title: Terminal output cannot forge shell-integration command entries or exit codes
statement: Each terminal session mints a random nonce, passes it only to its bash integration (which moves it into a readonly shell variable and unsets the environment variable before ~/.bashrc runs), and the session's marker scanner accepts only OSC 133 E, C and D sequences that carry that nonce. Any other 133 sequence in the output, including the nonce-less form, is ignored. Jobs get no nonce, so their output never announces an integration.
failure_mode: The scanner accepted any ESC ] 133;E/C/D sequence in PTY output, so cat of a crafted file or a printf created process-center entries such as 'rm -rf /' with invented exit codes, and could close a real command early as unknown. The marker tests only checked that well-formed markers parse; nothing fed the scanner markers the shell did not print. The deciding test now prints forged markers from a real integrated shell and asserts no entry and the real exit status.
notes: Audit AGT-024. Residual: a stream that replays this session's own raw output (e.g. cat of a saved transcript of the same session) can replay a valid nonce; a fresh nonce per session bounds it to that session. layer: test-suite
